campaign: keyv / cacheable npm supply-chain worm (Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again)

package_list_sources.name: socket.dev
package_list_sources.provenance: Primary feed. Supplied by the company incident-response team handling this campaign; the CSV is the machine-readable export of Socket's public incident page.
package_list_sources.notes: Live feed, updated minute-by-minute. One row per package@version; scoped names split into Namespace+Name. Includes non-npm ecosystems (golang). The HTML incident page sits behind Cloudflare bot protection and is not fetchable by script - read it in a browser. The /api/public/ CSV path returns 200 to plain HTTP clients and is what this skill consumes.

package_list_sources.provenance: Secondary feed. Public Wiz Research IOC repository, cited in their campaign write-up; kept as an independent cross-check and as failover if the primary feed is unreachable.

package_list_sources.name: datadog
package_list_sources.provenance: Datadog Security Labs IOC repo, published alongside their payload teardown. Layout: ecosystem,package,versions.
package_list_sources.notes: Third independent source. Their write-up is the deepest public payload analysis and is the origin of most host-persistence IOCs in this profile.

known_benign_collisions.reason: Legitimate Unicode general-category data table. IOC is specifically node_modules/keyv/Math_Symbol.js.
Legitimate motion library gesture helper. IOC is setup.mjs inside .claude/ or .vscode/.

payload_size_hints.note: Second stage is an obfuscated ~728 KB blob. Legitimate files of this name (regenerate-unicode-properties Unicode tables) are ~1 KB - a ~700x separation, so size catches variants whose hash is not yet published.
Same second-stage payload under its alternate name.

campaign_facts.infection_chain: preinstall hook (setup.mjs) -> downloads standalone Bun runtime -> executes obfuscated ~728 KB second stage (Math_Symbol.js)
campaign_facts.exfil_method: AES-256-GCM under an operator public key, delivered to threat-actor GitHub repos and DNS-resolved destinations
campaign_facts.provenance_bypass: keyv@6.0.0 shipped with PASSING npm provenance (signed SLSA attestation): the legitimate release workflow built already-trojanized source, so signature verification succeeded on malware. Provenance/attestation checks do NOT detect this campaign.
campaign_facts.propagation: worm republishes trojanized versions of every package the stolen npm token can reach, minting fresh sigstore provenance for each
campaign_facts.bun_reuse: The loader accepts ANY already-installed bun that runs (it does not require v1.3.13) and only downloads Bun into a bun-dl-* temp dir when bun is ABSENT. On a host with Bun installed, absence of bun-dl-* is therefore NOT evidence of non-infection.
campaign_facts.c2_code_execution: Primary C2 response is eval'd unsandboxed and unsigned, so the implant is a general remote code-execution channel, not only a credential stealer.
campaign_facts.first_malicious_state: 2026-08-04T09:02:37Z (commit 29c773...), ~32 min before the keyv@6.0.0 publish at 09:35:00.763Z

runtime_markers.notes: Single-instance lock lives under the OS temp dir; env guard prevents detached-child recursion.

ide_cross_wiring.detail: Malicious SessionStart hook runs node .vscode/setup.mjs - a Claude hook pointing into .vscode/ is anomalous.
Malicious folderOpen task runs node .claude/setup.mjs - a VS Code task pointing into .claude/ is anomalous.

exact_scripts_signatures.detail: Worm REPLACES the entire scripts object with exactly this when republishing a stolen package.

injected_ci_artifacts.detail: Created to exfiltrate ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}; run and branch are deleted afterwards but audit-log/artifact records may remain.

_path_pattern_policy: Only filenames with NO legitimate use at that path belong here (setup.mjs, math_init.js). Files that are normally legitimate (.claude/settings.json, .vscode/tasks.json) must be confirmed by hash or cross-wiring instead - confirming them by path would flag every developer's IDE config.
